newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business confidence buoyant in April -- Chamber.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business confidence buoyant in April -- Chamber.

text.p: Business optimism was at its highest peak during April since late 1995, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce said on Monday, buoyed by steady economic growth with litle or no sign of inflation.

The corporate lobby group's Business Confidence Index climbed to 56.5 in April from 52.3 in December, when the last such survey was conducted of business prospects for economic growth, employment and sales over the next six months.

"In spite of higher interest rates -- and the looming threat of future increases -- business owners and managers are more optimistic due to the continued strong levels of consumer spending," said Robert Barr, the chamber's deputy chief economist.
A total of 4,249 companies were surveyed.
The last time there was a higher index reading was in October 1995 when the index hit 56.8, the chamber said.
